To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have identified a new HDAC3 interactant, PROX1, that controls a gene program regulating hepatic lipid homeostasis.
HDAC3 is an important mediator of hepatic triglyceride content, and that the HDAC3-PRX1 complex acts as a corepressor module to repress the expression of genes involved in hepatic lipid metabolism.

HDAC3 is recruited to the liver genome by HNF4α, where it forms a complex with PROX1 to repress a program of genes regulating lipid metabolism, and hepatic ablation of either HDAC3 or PROX1 leads to increased hepatic triglyceride content.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of the HDAC3 interactors and their role in the regulation of hepatic lipid homeostasis.
the molecular mechanisms that regulate hepatic lipid homeostasis.
the role of HDAC3 as a key mediator of hepatic triglyceride metabolism.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the HDAC3–NCoR–SMRT complex and the HDAC3/PROX1 module act in concert to regulate hepatic lipid metabolism.
the authors show that HDAC 3 and PROX 1 interact and co-localize extensively with HNF 4α on chromatin and that the loss of either component increases hepatic triglyceride content.
the authors provide evidence that HDACT interacts with PROX and that HDAC3- PROX1 module controls lipid homeostasis.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we identified a new coregulatory complex, HDAC3–NCoR–PROX1, that is critical to the regulation of HNF4α target genes and lipid homeostasis in the liver.
HDAC3, in concert with the corepressor PROX1, is a critical regulator of hepatic triglyceride metabolism.
the HDAC3- PROX1 module is an important component in the regulation of hepatic lipid homeostasis.
The main takeaway from our work is that
specific combinations of transcriptional regulators and corepressors are required for the fine-tuning of metabolic pathways in the liver.
the HDAC3–Prox1 module is critical to control lipid homeostasis in the liver.
specific combinations of transcription regulators and co-regulators play a critical role in fine tuning metabolism.
